primary_diagnosis_treated: Chronic Kidney Disease, mixed diabetic & hypertensive etiology
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management)

medications.purpose: Renal protection and blood pressure control in CKD
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line ACE‑I/ARB for CKD with proteinuria or hypertension

medications.purpose: Blood pressure optimisation and reduction of proteinuria
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends thiazide diuretic as part of BP target strategy

medications.purpose: Adjunct antihypertensive to achieve BP target <140/90 mmHg
medications.nice_justification: NG203 advises CCB addition when BP not at target with ACE‑I + thiazide

medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction in all CKD patients
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends high‑intensity statin (e.g., atorvastatin 20 mg) for CKD

medications.purpose: Slow CKD progression and reduce cardiovascular events
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line SGLT2‑i for CKD with ACR ≥2.6 mg/mmol or eGFR 20‑45 mL/min/1.73 m² (TA775)

interactions_checked.interaction: Amlodipine inhibits CYP3A4, modestly increasing atorvastatin plasma concentrations
interactions_checked.action: Monitor CK and liver enzymes after 4–12 weeks; consider dose reduction if toxicity develops

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined use raises risk of euglycaemic keto‑acidosis and hypoglycaemia
interactions_checked.action: Discontinue insulin before initiating dapagliflozin; re‑evaluate glycaemic status

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – NICE NG203 SGLT2‑i indication requires eGFR ≥20 mL/min/1.73 m²; assume eGFR ≥20 pending lab confirmation
Albumin‑creatinine ratio (ACR) not provided – SGLT2‑i also requires ACR ≥2.6 mg/mmol; assume proteinuria present based on urine dipstick, confirm quantitatively
Serum potassium not available – needed to safely continue ACE‑I and monitor after starting dapagliflozin; assume within normal range pending test
Liver function tests not available – required before initiating high‑intensity atorvastatin; assume normal pending test
HbA1c recorded as 3.1 % (implausible) – likely pre‑diabetes; repeat HbA1c to confirm glycaemic status before any glucose‑lowering therapy
Allergy status not documented – verify no hypersensitivity to ACE‑I, statin, or SGLT2‑i
treatment_summary: Continue ACE‑I (lisinopril), thiazide (hydrochlorothiazide) and CCB (amlodipine) for blood pressure control; replace low‑dose simvastatin with high‑intensity atorvastatin 20 mg for cardiovascular risk reduction; add dapagliflozin 10 mg daily to slow CKD progression, provided eGFR ≥20 and ACR ≥2.6 mg/mmol. Discontinue insulin as it is not indicated for pre‑diabetes and poses hypoglycaemia risk, especially with dapagliflozin. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, CK, liver enzymes, and glycaemic status according to NG203 recommendations.
